nodes.name: Every 15 minutes
nodes.notes:
Fifteen minutes is the worst-case time to hear that the host started filling up — 96 scans a day, each one HTTP request and zero tokens.

Tighten to */5 if you want; the cost is the same and the probe is idempotent. Widening past an hour is the real risk: disk does not fill gradually when a Docker build goes wrong, it fills in minutes.

This workflow lives INSIDE the stack it watches. It catches a filling disk, not a dead server — for that you want an outside pinger.

nodes.name: Igor: scan host
nodes.notes:
THE CHEAP HALF — nothing to edit here. One SSH round trip to the host, reading disk %, free space, inodes, memory, swap and the Docker footprint, compared against the thresholds in Igor's config (LIFEBOAT_WATCH_PCT / LIFEBOAT_CRITICAL_PCT / LIFEBOAT_MEM_*). No LLM, so a healthy host costs nothing.

The thresholds live in Igor, NOT here, on purpose: a second copy in n8n is a second thing to keep in step, and this workflow has no tests.

onError continueRegularOutput: an unreachable host must not fail the run — the Gate inspects the response and handles it.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.notes:
The cost boundary — everything downstream spends money, everything upstream does not. On a healthy host this returns no items and the branch stops.

It also writes the `intent`. Escalation, critical, still-unhealthy and recovery are four different instructions to Orion; giving them one shared wording is how a recovery notice arrives sounding like a fire.

nodes.name: Igor: trigger Orion
nodes.notes:
THE EXPENSIVE HALF — one agentic turn, and only on an edge. Nothing to edit.

Every number the probe read rides in the payload, so Orion does not re-fetch what this poll already paid for.

No onError, deliberately: a failure must kill the branch BEFORE the ack, leaving the level uncommitted so the next poll reports the same escalation again. A duplicate push is recoverable; a swallowed 'the disk is full' is not.

nodes.name: Igor: ack level
nodes.notes:
Records that the owner has now been told about THIS level, so the next poll stays quiet until the situation actually moves.

Deliberately AFTER the trigger: committing first would lose the escalation whenever the notify call failed. On the blind-probe alert path there is no level to ack and this is a harmless no-op.
